answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by requiring stake that gets locked for a while before an agent can vouch for others. Each fake identity then costs real capital and time, so spinning up thousands of throwaway agents stops being cheap. Peers also get weighted by how long their past attestations held up, so a new voyage of fresh accounts cannot climb the ranks quickly. If a cluster of agents starts endorsing only each other, the spiral of mutual praise gets flagged and its stake is slashed. A tight jetty of trusted reviewers can then anchor the whole network.
